policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV's 'he shall live' is compatible with both the qere וְחָיָה and the ketiv יחיה and supplies no mapped textual note distinguishing them; retain the qere base fallback.
ASV reads 'because of the evil of your doings,' selecting the second-person qere מַעַלְלֵיכֶם; the mapped textual-variant note explicitly identifies 'their' as the other reading.
